newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares end lower, confidence weak.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end lower, confidence weak.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed down slightly on Friday with continuing bearish sentiment keeping investors away from the market, brokers said.
The B share index lost 0.57 points or 0.42 percent to 135.40 on turnover of HK$44 million against Thursday's HK$53 million.
The A share market erased early losses to end up 3.36 points or 0.82 percent at 411.62 on a technical rebound after heavy losses in the past three consecutive sessions, brokers said.
Turnover on the A share market contracted to 5.7 billion yuan from 6.6 billion on Thursday.
"The B share market's recent poor performance coupled with shrinking turnover indicate weakening investor confidence," a trader at J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
"It was a day dominated by volatile trading among small investors," the trader said.

Analysts said stagnant trading would extend into early next week ahead of the listing of large Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd, which is set to float 400 million B shares on the Shenzhen bourse next Tuesday.
They said the expected modest debut by Bengang due to weak market sentiment and limited optimism over China's steel industry is likely to further dampen confidence.

"Shanghai's B share newcomer Jinan Qinqi Motorcycle Co 900946.SS has now traded below its issue price, which set a bad example for forthcoming new B share listings," a Shenzhen J&A Securities analyst said.
Brokers said both the city's A and B share markets remained overshadowed by Thursday's sharp declines.
The A share market moved into positive territory on Friday only because it had fallen much more sharply recently than B shares, brokers said.
"Investors are refraining from building new positions as they see many uncertainties ahead," an analyst with China Guotai Securities said.
Rumours that Beijing was hammering out details on the implementation of the general anti-speculation policies announced in May and June sent share prices sharply lower on Thursday, brokers said.
"The market is likely to see careful selective buying in the corporate interim results reporting period up to the end of next month," the Guotai analyst said.
Brokers said the A share market's performance next week will largely hinge on whether there will be any negative news over the weekend.

On the B share market, the biggest loser was Shenzhen Textile, sinking HK$0.27 or 9.68 percent to HK$2.52 on volume of only 3,600 shares. On the A share market, China Zhenhua registered the heaviest loss of 1.45 yuan to close at its 10-percent limit-down at 13.04 yuan on profit-taking.
